hints.title: Cost Constrained Window Obstacle
hints.text: Changing character s[i] to t[i] costs abs(ord(s[i]) - ord(t[i])). How can you find the longest window whose total transformation cost does not exceed maxCost?

hints.title: Monotonic Window Cost Invariant
hints.text: As right pointer expands, total cost increases monotonically. When total cost exceeds maxCost, advance left pointer to restore validity.

hints.title: Dynamic Window Expansion Procedure
hints.text: Initialize left = 0, currCost = 0, maxLen = 0. For right in range(len(s)): add abs(ord(s[right]) - ord(t[right])) to currCost. While currCost > maxCost: subtract abs(ord(s[left]) - ord(t[left])) from currCost; left += 1. Update maxLen = max(maxLen, right - left + 1). Return maxLen.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def equalSubstring(self, s: str, t: str, maxCost: int) -> int:
        left = 0
        curr_cost = 0
        max_len = 0
        for right in range(len(s)):
            curr_cost += abs(ord(s[right]) - ord(t[right]))
            while curr_cost > maxCost:
                curr_cost -= abs(ord(s[left]) - ord(t[left]))
                left += 1
            max_len = max(max_len, right - left + 1)
        return max_len
```

variables: N: length of string s and t (1 <= N <= 10^5)
complexity.notes: Dynamic sliding window advancing left and right at most N times in O(1) space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing all O(N^2) substrings and computing conversion costs takes quadratic time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizing that transformation cost is non-negative, enabling standard two-pointer dynamic expansion.
